subject: gk
question: Against which oppressive law did Mahatma Gandhi launch a movement in 1919 that made him a truly national leader?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the British government in March 1919, which aimed at curbing the growing nationalist upsurge in India.
 
• It authorized the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism living in British India for up to two years without a trial.
 
• This Act allowed the British to arrest and detain individuals without any judicial process and suppress press freedom.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi launched a movement against this oppressive law, leading to widespread protests and strikes, making him a national leader.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morley-Minto Reforms**

 
 
• The Morley-Minto Reforms, also known as the Indian Councils Act 1909, introduced separate electorates for Muslims and provided for the inclusion of Indians in the governance of British India.
 
• It was an attempt to appease the demands of Indians for greater participation in the government.
 
 
 
• **Salt Tax**
 
 
• The Salt Tax was a tax levied on the production of salt, which was a basic necessity.
 
• This tax led to the famous Salt March by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 as part of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
 
 
 
• **Vernacular Press Act**
 
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 by Lord Lytton, aimed at curbing the freedom of the Indian language press.
 
• The act prohibited the publication of any material that could incite dissatisfaction or rebellion against the British government.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, gave the British government extraordinary powers to suppress subversive activities.
 
• It led to widespread unrest and was one of the precursors to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919, where hundreds of unarmed civilians were killed.
 
• The protests against the Rowlatt Act marked a significant moment in the Indian independence movement, bringing together people from different regions and backgrounds.
